# What's new

> **这页管什么**：指南自己的变更记录，少数几处解释了规则背后的理由——这些理由比规则本身有用。
>
> 来源：<https://developers.google.com/style/whats-new> · CC BY 4.0 · 本文件是**规则摘要**，非原文全文。

## Recent changes (as fetched, July 2026)

- Softened language about how inconsistent terminology affects translation costs.
- Clarified that inclusive-documentation guidance connects to avoiding figurative language, which can be ableist or unnecessarily graphic.
- Heading targets: `<a>` elements are now equally acceptable as `<section>` elements.
- Added guidance on contextualizing UI elements documented outside numbered procedures.

## April 2026

- Recommended the phrase "do the following" for introducing procedure lists.
- Added guidance to use italics sparingly; consolidated into a dedicated page.
- Recommended "selected" and "not selected" for checkbox states.
- Expanded exclamation-mark guidance: avoid except in rare cases.
- Created a dedicated page for mathematical notation.
- Distinguished a **page** (whole web page) from a **document** (explanatory text on a page).

## Rationale given for specific decisions

These are the rare cases where the guide explains itself. They are the most transferable part of the page.

- **Semicolons** (Sept 2022) — guidance strengthened against them because *screen readers may not clearly indicate them*.
- **External-link icon removed** (Nov 2023) — *readers and writers expressed confusion about the meaning and usage of the icon*.
- **Humor** (May 2022) — avoidance strengthened because *most humor is difficult to translate, and much humor is culturally specific*.
- **Lettered lists removed** (April 2022) — *the semantic distinction isn't in wide use, and lettered lists aren't supported in standard Markdown*.

## Pattern across years

Recurring themes: continual word-list refinement; increasing accessibility emphasis (directional language, screen-reader compatibility); progressive simplification; consolidation of scattered guidance into dedicated pages.
